problem: Google wanted a way to reach people on mobile phones.
title: Google acquires Android Inc. and builds an open mobile operating system
context: Android started as a digital camera software company and shifted to mobile phones as standalone cameras declined.
decision_made: Acquire Android Inc. in 2005, reportedly for about $50 million, and back an open-source phone OS.
action_taken: Founder Andy Rubin joined Google; the first Android phone, the T-Mobile G1, shipped in late 2008.
observed_outcome: IDC put Android at about 68 percent of global smartphone shipments in Q2 2012, and later figures were near 80 percent by one source.
lessons: An early, inexpensive acquisition of a small team can anchor a very large platform.
limitations: The $50 million price is reported, not confirmed. Closing dates differ (May or July 2005). Market share figures come from different firms and years and are not directly comparable.

claims.claim_text: Google acquired Android Inc. in 2005, reportedly for about $50 million.
IDC put Android at 68 percent of the Q2 2012 global smartphone market.
